title: Something She'll Actually Like

pre.en: What did Lily really want for her birthday?
pre.zh: Lily 生日真正想要的是什么？

intro: 这是一段对话：Lily 的生日快到了，小陈和 Priya 在伦敦一家店一家店地逛，商量给她寄什么。读的时候留意最高级：the most boring、one of the worst、the biggest … I know、the cheapest、the easiest——挑礼物就是在挑「最」。最后小陈的手机里有个意外。

sentences.en: Right, Lily's birthday is in ten days.
sentences.zh: 好了，Lily 还有十天就过生日了。
sentences.speaker: Priya

sentences.en: So what's the plan?
sentences.zh: 你打算怎么办？

sentences.en: The parcel has to go to China by Friday, or it won't get there in time.
sentences.zh: 包裹周五前必须寄去中国，不然就赶不上了。
sentences.speaker: Chen

sentences.en: I've got fifty pounds and no ideas.
sentences.zh: 我手上有 50 英镑，脑子里一个主意都没有。

sentences.en: Come on, you must have something in mind.
sentences.zh: 得了吧，你心里总该有点想法吧？
sentences.speaker: Priya

sentences.en: A scarf, maybe?
sentences.zh: 围巾，怎么样？
sentences.speaker: Chen

sentences.en: A scarf?
sentences.zh: 围巾？
sentences.speaker: Priya

sentences.en: That's the most boring present I've ever heard of.
sentences.zh: 这是我听过最没劲的礼物了。

sentences.en: It's what people grab at the airport.
sentences.zh: 那是人家在机场随手抓的东西。

sentences.en: OK, a phone case, then.
sentences.zh: 好吧，那买个手机壳。
sentences.speaker: Chen

sentences.en: She drops her phone about twice a day.
sentences.zh: 她一天差不多要摔两回手机。

sentences.en: Even worse — a phone case is one of the worst presents ever.
sentences.zh: 那更糟——手机壳是最差劲的礼物之一。
sentences.speaker: Priya

sentences.en: What's she into these days?
sentences.zh: 她最近喜欢什么？

sentences.en: Baking, I think.
sentences.zh: 烘焙吧，我觉得。
sentences.speaker: Chen

sentences.en: And reading, when she has time on her hands.
sentences.zh: 还有看书，前提是她闲下来。

sentences.en: Which isn't often, because she works nights.
sentences.zh: 可她很少闲，因为她上夜班。

sentences.en: Well, we're on a budget, so let's be clever about it.
sentences.zh: 嗯，咱们预算有限，得动动脑子。
sentences.speaker: Priya

sentences.en: The bookshop on Neal Street has the biggest cookbook section I know.
sentences.zh: 尼尔街那家书店的菜谱区，是我知道的最大的。

sentences.en: Right, that's the third bookshop in an hour, and every cookbook's heavier than the last.
sentences.zh: 行了，一个钟头逛了三家书店，菜谱一本比一本重。
sentences.speaker: Chen

sentences.en: Posting one to China would cost more than the book itself.
sentences.zh: 寄一本去中国，邮费比书还贵。

sentences.en: Fine, I'll meet you halfway.
sentences.zh: 好吧，咱们各让一步。
sentences.speaker: Priya

sentences.en: No books, but no scarves either.
sentences.zh: 不买书，但也不买围巾。

sentences.en: And no candles.
sentences.zh: 也不买蜡烛。
sentences.speaker: Chen

sentences.en: The cheapest one in that last shop was £38, and it smelled like a hotel bathroom.
sentences.zh: 刚才那家店最便宜的蜡烛都要 38 英镑，闻着还像酒店卫生间。

sentences.en: Listen, you can't go wrong with something she can eat.
sentences.zh: 听我的，送吃的总不会错。
sentences.speaker: Priya

sentences.en: Good tea, biscuits, chocolate...
sentences.zh: 好茶、饼干、巧克力……

sentences.en: And food's the easiest thing to wrap up.
sentences.zh: 而且吃的最好包。

sentences.en: True.
sentences.zh: 也是。
sentences.speaker: Chen

sentences.en: She snacks on biscuits all through her night shifts.
sentences.zh: 她上夜班的时候，饼干一直没离过嘴。

sentences.en: There you go.
sentences.zh: 这不就得了。
sentences.speaker: Priya

sentences.en: Let's get on with it — the post office closes at half five.
sentences.zh: 赶紧办吧，邮局五点半就关门了。

sentences.en: And we'd get more done if you put your phone away.
sentences.zh: 还有，你把手机收起来，咱们效率能高点。

sentences.en: Hang on.
sentences.zh: 等等。
sentences.speaker: Chen

sentences.en: I've just come across a message from Lily, from three weeks ago.
sentences.zh: 我刚翻到 Lily 三个星期前发的一条消息。

sentences.en: She sends about forty a day, so they just pile up.
sentences.zh: 她一天发四十来条，消息全堆在那儿没看。

sentences.en: It's a link to a cookbook, and it says, "This one, please!"
sentences.zh: 是一本菜谱的链接，后面写着：「就要这本！」

sentences.en: You're joking.
sentences.zh: 不是吧。
sentences.speaker: Priya

sentences.en: So she told you exactly what she wanted.
sentences.zh: 所以她早就把想要什么明明白白告诉你了。

sentences.en: Well, it's the thought that counts.
sentences.zh: 嗯，送礼看心意嘛。

sentences.en: Especially hers.
sentences.zh: 特别是她自己的心意。

cards.note: 英式说法；美式多说 package。
to have an idea or plan about what you want
cards.tip: 店员常问 Do you have anything in mind?（您有看中的吗？）；in 不能换成 on。
cards.example: I'd like a new sofa, but I don't have a colour in mind yet.

cards.note: 复数是 scarves。
to be very interested in an activity or subject and enjoy it
cards.tip: 口语说法；后面接名词或 doing：be into running。问别人喜好时 into 放在句末：What are you into?
cards.example: My brother is really into old cameras.

cards.zh: 闲着没事；有大把空闲时间
cards.note: to have a lot of free time and not much to do
cards.tip: your 跟着主语变：she has time on her hands；hands 用复数。
cards.example: Now that I'm retired, I have a lot of time on my hands.

cards.note: having only a limited amount of money to spend
cards.tip: 常说 be on a budget、travel on a budget；a tight budget 是「预算很紧」。
cards.example: If you're on a budget, the market is cheaper than the supermarket.

cards.note: 英式也说 cookery book。
to agree to some of what another person wants so that you can both agree
香薰蜡烛是 scented candle。

cards.text: you can't go wrong with sth
cards.note: used to say that something is a safe choice and will not disappoint
cards.tip: you 在这里泛指「谁都」，不是专指对方；with 后面接名词。
cards.example: If you don't know what to cook, you can't go wrong with pasta.

cards.note: 英式说法；美式的 biscuit 是一种松软的小面包。
to cover something in paper, especially a present
cards.tip: 代词放中间：wrap it up；在会议里 Let's wrap up 是「收尾、结束」。
cards.example: I wrapped the present up in old newspaper.

cards.note: to eat small amounts of a particular food between meals
cards.tip: snack 在这里是动词，介词用 on。
cards.example: I try to snack on fruit instead of crisps.

cards.note: 上夜班也可以说 work nights。
to start or continue doing a job, especially after a delay

cards.zh: 干成更多的事；效率更高
cards.note: to finish more work in the same amount of time
to put something back in the place where it is usually kept
口语，比 wait 随意；打电话时 Hang on a sec 是「稍等」。
to find something or meet someone when you are not looking for them
to become a large amount, often because you have not dealt with it
cards.tip: 不及物，主语就是堆起来的东西：The dishes piled up.
cards.example: My emails always pile up when I'm on holiday.

cards.zh: 礼轻情意重；心意最重要
cards.note: used to say that a present is nice because someone thought about you, even if it is small or not perfect
cards.tip: 固定说法，count 在这里是「重要、算数」，不是「数数」；常带点安慰或打趣。
cards.example: The cake looked terrible, but it's the thought that counts.
